extracted.intended_audience: organizational leaders, HR professionals, culture consultants, and business readers interested in corporate culture
extracted.subtask_description: A blog-case analysis of Uber’s historical company culture failures and lessons for designing, defining, and enforcing corporate core values and people practices. Focuses on how leadership, HR, and value-definition affect organizational behavior and public trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core values need clear descriptive behaviors
rubrics_metrics.description: When a CoreVal is too vague and lacks the descriptive behaviors that define the value, it's left open to abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide in-depth descriptive behaviors for each core value so employees know acceptable behaviors and limits; the post contrasts Uber’s original one-liners with the new list of core values 'with in-depth descriptive behaviors.' Example anti-pattern: 'toe-stepping' being vague and therefore misused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Values must align with actual actions (no just-slogans)
rubrics_metrics.description: Uber’s cultural deterioration serves as a quintessential example of the consequences when a company espouses core values but fails to uphold them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid empty one-liners like 'Always be hustlin'' or 'Be yourself' without substance; ensure values are operationalized so they guide real decisions and behaviors rather than just serve as marketing copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent misuse of values as justification for bad behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Toe-stepping' was meant to encourage employees to share ideas regardless of seniority, but too often it was used as an excuse for being an asshole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design values and descriptive behaviors that cannot be twisted to justify harassment, bullying, or rule-bending; monitor how values are cited in internal debates and discipline misuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical and lawful use of user data; avoid evading regulators
rubrics_metrics.description: Uber used a technique called 'greyballing' that 'used data collected from the Uber app to evade authorities' — an action greenlighted internally but subject to DOJ inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data practices should be consistent with stated values (e.g., 'Celebrate cities'); ensure legal compliance and ethical review of product features that affect users, regulators, or public institutions. Anti-pattern: technical workarounds that deliberately deceive regulators or users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership must model empathy, accountability, and inspiring behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Kalanick's defensive response to a driver’s complaint demonstrated a lack of empathy and contradicted the value 'Inspiring leadership.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaders set the tone for culture through words and actions; expect leaders to show empathy, take responsibility, and behave consistently with professed values. Failure at the top accelerates cultural collapse and loss of public trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: HR must respond effectively to harassment and protect employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Susan Fowler experienced sexual harassment; HR advised her to change teams and her complaints were repeatedly dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have processes that take complaints seriously, protect complainants from retaliation, investigate thoroughly, and deliver appropriate remedies. Ignoring or minimizing reports damages employee safety and reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure, report, and be transparent about people & culture metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Uber began publishing annual People & Culture Reports and transparently sharing them with the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular public reporting on culture metrics (diversity, retention, safety incidents, etc.) helps rebuild trust and holds the organization accountable. Transparency is a corrective tool after cultural failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commit to diversity, equity, and inclusion with actionable goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Female representation at Uber fell from 25% to 3% during the period described, illustrating systemic sexism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track representation and retention metrics, investigate causes of demographic declines, implement targeted policies to improve inclusion, and measure outcomes. Anti-pattern: treating diversity as a PR line without substantive change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforce values through governance, accountability, and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Shareholders demanded Kalanick step down because 'the cultural values of Uber need to be transformed to embrace transparency, diversity and social responsibility alongside growth and the bottom line.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When values are violated at scale, governance interventions (leadership change, board action, policy overhaul) may be necessary to restore alignment and public trust. Use concrete consequences to signal seriousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leaders should engage with frontline/user experience to inform decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Khosrowshahi moonlighted as an Uber and UberEats driver to better understand the driver app and driver complaints, informing product and cultural changes tied to the value 'Trip obsessed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage leaders to experience products/services and frontline work to surface real problems and empathize with workers and customers; tie those insights to concrete product and policy changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft core values that are unique, memorable, and specific
rubrics_metrics.description: The post praises the new values as 'unique, memorable, and clear' while warning that some values still need clearer definition given past abuses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for values that are distinctive and easily recalled, but accompany them with specific behaviors, examples, and boundaries so they guide daily decisions rather than being rhetorical.
